title: Perfect in its words, detailed in its meaning.
subtitle: A pause before a surah that turned hair gray
then: The Prophet ﷺ was asked why his hair had turned gray. He named {trap}Surah Hud and its sisters{/trap}. It opens with letters whose meaning is known to Allah, then describes the Book: {idea}firm in its words, detailed in its meaning{/idea}, from One who knows how every matter ends.
now: You open the app in a waiting room, half distracted, thumb ready to scroll. The surah starts with three letters you cannot explain. {idea}Let them slow you down.{/idea} What follows was heavy enough to gray the hair of the one who received it.
old: I can skim the Quran like any other text.
new: This was sent by One who knows where everything ends, so it deserves my full attention.
try: Before you read any surah today, put the phone face down for ten seconds and just breathe.

title: The whole Book points to one thing.
subtitle: Worship Allah alone, said by a warner and bringer of news
then: Ibn Kathir links this to the day the Prophet ﷺ stood on Mount Safa and called Quraysh. He asked if they would believe him about riders attacking at dawn. They said {reward}we have never known you to lie{/reward}. Then he said: {trap}I am a warner before a severe punishment.{/trap}
now: Think of the friend who texts you that the road ahead is flooded. You do not argue, you turn around, and you thank them. {idea}The message is a warning and good news at the same time.{/idea} It all comes back to one line: worship none but Allah.
old: Warnings in religion are just meant to scare me.
new: A warning from someone who never lied to me is a kindness, and it comes with good news.
try: Say la ilaha illa Allah slowly three times today and think about what it rules out in your life.

title: Ask forgiveness, turn back, and life itself gets better.
subtitle: Forgiveness for the past, repentance for what comes next
then: Ibn Kathir explains the order: {idea}seek forgiveness for past sins, then turn away from future ones{/idea}. The promise is a good life in this world for a set term, and grace in the Hereafter. But {trap}turning away brings fear of a Great Day{/trap}.
now: You keep putting off the clean start, as if going back to Allah means giving up everything fun. Meanwhile the guilt sits in your chest every night before sleep. {reward}The verse says the opposite: turning back is what makes life good.{/reward}
old: If I get serious about repenting, my life will get smaller.
new: Forgiveness and a fresh turn are what open up a good life, not what shrink it.
try: Tonight, say astaghfirullah ten times, then name one habit you want to leave behind.

title: Every road ends back with Him.
subtitle: The return, and the power behind it
then: The opening message ends here: your return is to Allah on the Day of Judgement. Ibn Kathir notes He is able to bring creation back again. He says {reward}the previous verse encourages hope{/reward}, and {trap}this one encourages fear{/trap}.
now: You plan the next five years: the move, the promotion, the house. Every plan has an end date you do not control. {idea}Hope and fear both keep you walking straight.{/idea} The trip home is the one appointment that is certain.
old: I will think about the return when I am older.
new: Every plan I make is on a road that leads back to Him, so I can hope and be careful at once.
try: Write down one goal for this year, and next to it, how you would want it to look on the Day you return.

title: Folding in on yourself does not hide you from Him.
subtitle: Covering up, and the One who knows the heart

row.title: if I cover it, it is hidden

then: Ibn Abbas described people who were so shy of the open sky that they bent over and covered their heads even in private moments. The verse answers: {idea}even when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows{/idea}. {trap}There is no angle of hiding from Him.{/trap}
now: You lock the door, pull the blanket up, and scroll something you would not want anyone to see. Or you hide a resentment so well that even you forget it is there. {idea}He knows what is in the chest.{/idea} That is also why He can heal it.
old: If nobody can see it, it does not really count.
new: Nothing I hide is hidden from Him, and the One who sees it is the One who can fix it.
try: Tell Allah one thing in private dua today that you have never said out loud.

title: Every creature's meal is already on His list.
subtitle: Provision, home, and resting place, all recorded

row.title: He provides
sub: the job is just a door

then: Ibn Kathir says Allah is responsible for {reward}the provision of every creature{/reward}, small or large, on land or in the sea. Ibn Abbas said He knows where it lives and {idea}where it will die{/idea}. All of it is written in a clear Book.
now: Payday is still a week away and the account is low. You lie awake doing the math again. A pigeon outside your window has no bank account at all. {reward}Its meal is on His list, and so is yours.{/reward}
old: If I stop worrying about money for one second, everything will fall apart.
new: My provision is written and carried by Allah; my job is to work, not to carry the whole weight.
try: Next time you eat today, pause and say: this was written for me before I was born.

title: Not who does the most, but who does it best.
subtitle: Why the heavens and earth were made
then: Ibn Kathir points out that Allah did not say {trap}who does the most{/trap}, but {idea}who is best in deeds{/idea}. A deed counts when it is sincere for Allah and follows the way of the Prophet ﷺ. Those who heard about life after death called it magic.
now: You fill the day with tasks to feel productive: the checklist, the extra hours, the busy look. Then one small act done with a clean heart outweighs them all. {idea}Quality, not quantity.{/idea}
old: The more I do, the better I am.
new: Allah looks at how sincere and right my deeds are, not how many I can stack up.
try: Pick one thing you do today and do it slowly, well, and only for Allah.

title: A delay is not a cancellation.
subtitle: Mocking the warning because it has not come yet

row.title: nothing happened, so it is fine

then: The surah introduction says the delay was {reward}a respite granted by His grace{/reward}, so people might mend their ways. Instead the polytheists asked mockingly {trap}what is holding it back?{/trap} Ibn Kathir says rejection and doubt had become their nature.
now: You skipped the warning light on the dashboard for months and the car still runs. So you joke about it. {idea}The extra time was the gift, not proof that the warning was wrong.{/idea}
old: Nothing bad has happened yet, so I must be fine.
new: The time I still have is mercy, given so I can change before it runs out.
try: Think of one warning you keep laughing off in your own life. Take one small step on it today.

title: One loss and he forgets every gift before it.
subtitle: Despair when a blessing is taken back
then: Ibn Kathir describes a trait of people, except the believers Allah has mercy on. {trap}When hardship follows blessing, a person despairs{/trap} and acts as if he never saw any good. He loses all hope of relief.
now: Three good years at the job, then one layoff email. Within a day you are saying your life has always been a mess. {idea}The years before were real gifts.{/idea} One closed door does not erase them.
old: Now that this is gone, nothing good ever happens to me.
new: What was taken was a gift to begin with, and the Giver has not gone anywhere.
try: Write down three good things from the last year that you forgot when things got hard.

title: Good times return and he thinks he earned them forever.
subtitle: Boasting when hardship lifts
then: Right after the despair comes the opposite swing. Once relief arrives, a person claims {trap}no harm will touch me again{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says he is pleased with what is in his hand, ungrateful to Allah, and {trap}boastful toward others{/trap}.
now: The test results come back clear, or the bonus lands. Within a week you are posting about how you hustled your way out and forgot the nights you begged Allah for help. {idea}Relief is a gift to thank for, not a trophy to show off.{/idea}
old: I got through that by myself, and I am safe now.
new: Relief came from Allah, and the right reply is thanks, not showing off.
try: Think of one hard time that ended. Thank Allah for it out loud today.

title: Patient in hardship, doing good in ease.
subtitle: The people who do not swing
then: After the two swings, the verse names the exception. Ibn Kathir says these are {idea}patient in hardship and do good in times of ease{/idea}. Even the prick of a thorn wipes away sins for a believer. {reward}Whatever comes, it is good for him.{/reward}
now: Some weeks the hospital corridor, some weeks the wedding hall. You do not control which week comes. {idea}You only choose how you meet it.{/idea} Patience in one, good deeds in the other, and both count.
old: My faith is strong when life is good and weak when it is hard.
new: Both seasons are chances: patience in the hard one, good deeds in the easy one.
try: Ask yourself which season you are in today, and do the one thing that fits it.

title: Their mocking should not make you hold back the message.
subtitle: When people demand treasure or an angel
then: The polytheists asked why no treasure or angel came with the Prophet ﷺ. Ibn Kathir says this verse {reward}comforted him{/reward}. He was only a warner, and the earlier messengers had been rejected too, yet {idea}they were patient until Allah's help came{/idea}.
now: You mention prayer in the family group chat and someone replies with a laughing emoji. Next time you stay quiet. {idea}Your part is to say it kindly. Their hearts are with Allah.{/idea}
old: If they mock what I say, I should stop saying it.
new: My job is to pass on the good honestly; results belong to Allah.
try: Share one beneficial thing with someone today, kindly, and let go of how they react.

title: If he made it up, bring ten like it.
subtitle: The challenge to anyone who calls it invented
then: When they said {trap}he forged it{/trap}, the answer was a challenge: bring ten surahs like it, and call anyone besides Allah for help. Ibn Kathir explains that {idea}the speech of the Lord is not like the speech of created beings{/idea}, just as His attributes are not like theirs.
now: You hear a confident voice online say the Quran is just old poetry. It sounds smart for a minute. {idea}The challenge has been open for centuries.{/idea} Let that sink in before you let the doubt sink in.
old: Maybe it is just a very clever human book.
new: An open challenge no one has met is a sign this speech is from beyond us.
try: Read one short surah today and notice one line you could never have written yourself.

title: Silence after the challenge is itself an answer.
subtitle: So will you submit?
then: Ibn Kathir says if they cannot reply, {idea}their inability is the proof{/idea} that this is speech from Allah, full of His knowledge, commands and prohibitions. Then the verse turns to them directly: {trap}will you then be Muslims?{/trap}
now: You have read the articles, watched the talks, nodded along. You already know. {idea}The verse ends with a question, not a lecture.{/idea} What is one thing you know is right and still have not done?
old: I believe it, so I am already fine.
new: Knowing it is from Allah should move me to submit, not just agree.
try: Pick one command you already know and have been delaying. Do a small part of it today.

title: Want only this world, and you get paid only here.
subtitle: Deeds done for worldly gain are paid in worldly coin
then: Ibn Abbas said those who show off are {trap}given their reward in this life{/trap}, so no one is wronged even a speck. Mujahid said it is about people who do deeds to be seen. Qatadah said the believer is {reward}rewarded in this life and the next{/reward}.
now: You post the photo of the charity box, or pray a little longer when the in-laws are watching. The praise comes, and it feels good. {trap}That may be the whole payment.{/trap} The same deed done quietly for Allah gets paid twice.
old: As long as I do good, it does not matter who sees it.
new: The reason I do a good deed decides where it gets paid.
try: Do one good thing today that nobody will ever know about.

title: Deeds that looked impressive, but weighed nothing.
subtitle: What is left of work done only for the world
then: This verse finishes the thought of the previous one. Ibn Abbas said that a person who prays or fasts only for worldly benefit {trap}has his deed wasted{/trap}, since he only sought this world. Ibn Kathir adds that whoever strives for the Hereafter as a believer {reward}has his striving appreciated{/reward}.
now: You spend years building a reputation as the generous one at work. Every gift is noted, every favor remembered. {idea}Ask who it is really for.{/idea} The same hours can be turned toward Allah with one honest change of heart.
old: I have done so much good that I must be fine.
new: Good deeds only last if they were for Allah, so I keep checking why I do them.
try: Before one task today, pause and say quietly: this is for You, O Allah.

title: Your inner nature already recognizes the truth.
subtitle: Clear proof inside, a witness from outside
then: Ibn Kathir says the believer stands on {idea}the fitrah, the natural faith Allah placed in people{/idea}. Every child is born on it. The Quran then comes as a witness that matches it, and the Book of Musa came before as a guide. {trap}So be in no doubt about it.{/trap}
now: You look at a newborn in the hospital nursery and feel that something greater made this. No lecture told you that. {idea}That feeling is the first witness.{/idea} The Quran does not argue with it; it agrees with it.
old: Faith is something I have to be talked into.
new: My own nature already leans toward Allah, and the Quran confirms what it knows.
try: Spend two minutes today looking at something in nature and let your heart say who made it.

title: The worst wrong is lying about Allah.
subtitle: Two ways people stand before Him

row.title: His covering
sub: for those who turned to Him

then: Ibn Umar reported that Allah will draw the believer near, {reward}cover him from the people{/reward}, and remind him of his sins one by one. When he thinks he is ruined, Allah says: I hid these for you in the world and I forgive them today. {trap}The ones who lied about their Lord are named openly.{/trap}
now: You have messed up in ways nobody knows. Allah kept it hidden, day after day. {reward}That covering is a mercy you can lean into.{/reward} Never put words in Allah's name that He did not say, and keep asking Him to keep covering you.
old: My hidden sins mean I am already lost.
new: The One who has hidden my sins all this time can forgive them too, if I turn to Him.
try: Make a short dua today: O Allah, cover me in this world and the next.

title: Blocking the path, then calling it crooked.
subtitle: Turning others away from Allah's way
then: Ibn Kathir explains that these people {trap}kept others from the truth and the path of guidance{/trap}, and so kept them from Paradise. They wanted the path to look crooked. At the root, they did not believe in the Hereafter at all.
now: Your younger cousin starts praying and you joke that she has gone extreme. Or you make religion sound harsh when someone asks you a question. {idea}You can be the person who makes the path look easy.{/idea}
old: What I say about religion only affects me.
new: My words and jokes can push someone toward Allah or away, so I choose them with care.
try: Encourage one person today in a good thing they are trying to do.

title: Ears and eyes given, but never used for truth.
subtitle: No escape and no protector besides Allah
then: Ibn Kathir says they {trap}could not escape on earth{/trap}, and had no protector besides Allah. The Prophet ﷺ said Allah gives the oppressor respite until He seizes him. Their punishment is doubled because they were given {reward}hearing, sight and hearts{/reward} and used none of them for the truth.
now: You have ears for a podcast every commute, eyes for hours of screens a day. {idea}The same tools can turn toward what helps you.{/idea} Hearing is a gift, and so is noticing what you keep tuning out.
old: I am too busy to listen to reminders right now.
new: My hearing and sight are gifts I will be asked about, so I give some of them to the truth.
try: Swap one song or clip today for five minutes of Quran recitation.

title: They lost themselves, and their idols left them.
subtitle: What people invent besides Allah walks away
then: Ibn Kathir says what they invented, {trap}the rivals and idols besides Allah{/trap}, left them and did not help them at all. In fact those things harmed them. Those who were followed will disown those who followed them.
now: The influencer you quoted for years, the strategy you trusted, the status you chased. When the real test comes, {trap}none of it shows up for you.{/trap} {idea}Ask what you are leaning on that cannot hold you.{/idea}
old: The things I count on will always be there for me.
new: Anything I put in Allah's place will walk away from me when I need it most.
try: Name one thing you lean on more than Allah. Ask Him today to be your first support.

title: The worst trade anyone can make.
subtitle: The greatest losers, in the long run
then: Ibn Kathir calls this a {trap}transaction for the abode of the Hereafter{/trap}. They swapped the highest levels for the lowest, and {reward}nearness to Allah{/reward} for His anger. So it is no injustice that they are the greatest losers.
now: You would never trade a house for a phone case. Yet a long day can go by trading prayer time for scrolling, honesty for a small sale. {idea}Look at your trades the way a merchant does.{/idea}
old: Small choices today do not change the big picture.
new: My daily trades add up to the final account, so I want to stop trading the lasting for the cheap.
try: Notice one small trade today where you swap the better thing for the easier one, and switch it.

title: Believe, do good, and bow your heart to your Lord.
subtitle: The people of Paradise, forever
then: After describing the losers, the verse praises the believers. Ibn Kathir says {idea}their hearts believed and their limbs did good{/idea}, in words and actions. They will live in Paradise forever, {reward}and will see the Creator of the heavens and the earth{/reward}.
now: You finish your prayer and rush straight to the next notification. Or you give charity and quietly feel better than others. {idea}The verse adds a third thing: humility.{/idea} The deed lands better when the heart bows with it.
old: As long as I do the right things, my attitude does not matter.
new: Faith and good deeds are completed by a heart that humbles itself before Allah.
try: After your next prayer, stay seated one more minute and just thank Him, quietly.

title: Can the blind and the seeing ever be equal?
subtitle: The parable of the two groups
then: Ibn Kathir explains the parable. The one who rejects is {trap}blind to the truth and deaf to the proofs{/trap}. The believer {idea}sees the truth, tells it apart from falsehood, and follows the good{/idea}. Then the verse asks: will you not take heed?
now: Two coworkers hear the same rumor. One checks before sharing; the other forwards it to ten people. {idea}Same ears, different hearing.{/idea} Seeing clearly is a choice you make many times a day.
old: I see things the way they are.
new: Real sight is noticing the truth and following it, and I can ask Allah for more of it.
try: Before you share or react to anything today, stop and ask if it is true.

title: Nuh begins with the same clear warning.
subtitle: The first messenger to idol worshippers
then: The surah introduction says Allah teaches through the stories of past prophets. Ibn Kathir says Nuh was {idea}the first messenger sent to people of the earth{/idea} who worshipped idols. He warned them {trap}openly{/trap} against Allah's punishment if they kept worshipping others.
now: You hear the same advice from your grandmother, your teacher and a stranger at the mosque. It feels repetitive. {idea}Some messages repeat because they are true.{/idea} Nuh said what Hud and every prophet would say after him.
old: I have heard this reminder too many times already.
new: The message repeats across every prophet because it is the oldest truth there is.
try: Listen to one familiar reminder today as if you were hearing it for the first time.

title: Worship Allah alone, because I fear for you.
subtitle: A warning spoken out of care
then: Nuh's call was the same as the opening of this surah: {idea}worship none but Allah{/idea}. Ibn Kathir explains his words as: if you keep doing this, Allah will punish you severely in the Hereafter. Nuh says {reward}I fear for you{/reward}, the voice of someone who cares.
now: You see your brother slipping into a habit that is hurting him. You can lecture him, or you can say: I am worried about you. {reward}Fear for someone is a form of love.{/reward}
old: Warning someone means judging them.
new: A real warning comes from fear for the person, the way Nuh spoke to his people.
try: Tell one person you care about that you worry for them, gently and without blame.

title: They judged the message by who followed it.
subtitle: The chiefs looked down on the poor believers
then: The chiefs said Nuh was only human and {trap}only the lowest of us follow you{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says truth is not rejected because of the low status of its followers. Heraclius asked Abu Sufyan if the Prophet's ﷺ followers were noble or weak, then said {idea}the weak are the followers of the messengers{/idea}.
now: You dismiss an idea at work because the intern suggested it, then praise it when the manager repeats it. {idea}The truth does not change with the person saying it.{/idea} Check yourself before you check their rank.
old: If important people do not believe it, it is probably not true.
new: Truth is true whoever holds it, and the humble who follow it are the honored ones.
try: Listen fully today to someone you usually overlook, and take their point seriously.

title: Truth cannot be forced on a closed heart.
subtitle: Nuh refuses to push what they hate

row.title: his people
sub: they did not see its worth

then: Nuh's people had just called him an ordinary man followed by the lowest of them. He answered calmly. He had {idea}clear proof and a mercy from his Lord{/idea}, but it was hidden from their eyes, so they rushed to reject it. {trap}Should we force it on you while you hate it?{/trap}
now: Your brother scoffs every time you mention prayer at the family dinner. You feel the urge to win, to corner him with arguments until he gives in. {idea}Nuh did not force.{/idea} He kept the door open and his voice gentle.
old: If I care about someone, I should push until they agree.
new: My job is to make the truth clear; opening the heart is not mine to force.
try: Next time faith comes up with someone who resists, say one kind sentence and then let it rest.

title: He asked for no money and dropped no one.
subtitle: Nuh refuses to send the poor believers away

row.title: the chiefs
sub: too important to sit with them

then: The chiefs wanted Nuh to separate himself from the believers, because they felt {trap}too important to sit with them{/trap}. Quraysh later asked the Prophet ﷺ the same thing, to hold a private gathering just for the elite. Nuh said he took {reward}no payment, his reward was with Allah{/reward}, and he would not drive anyone away.
now: The masjid committee wants the big donor at the front and the quiet uncle who sweeps the floor out of sight. The work group chat has an inner circle. {idea}Nuh kept the poor believers at his side{/idea} even when it cost him the powerful.
old: To get the influential people on board, I may have to sideline the ordinary ones.
new: Those who turned to Allah keep their place, whatever it costs me with the powerful.
try: Sit with or message someone at your masjid or work whom others usually overlook.

title: Who would protect me if I pushed them out?
subtitle: Rejecting the humble has its own reckoning

row.title: Allah's displeasure
sub: no one shields me from it

then: Nuh kept answering the chiefs who wanted the weak believers gone. He turned their demand around: {trap}if I drove them away, who would help me against Allah?{/trap} Then he asked them to {idea}stop and think{/idea}.
now: You are planning the wedding guest list and someone says to cut the relatives who "do not fit." Or a manager asks you to quietly freeze out the new hire nobody likes. {idea}Ask Nuh's question.{/idea} Whose displeasure are you really avoiding?
old: Losing the approval of important people is the bigger risk.
new: Wronging a humble believer puts me against Allah, and no one can shield me from that.
try: Before you leave someone out of something this week, ask yourself who you are pleasing by it.

title: No treasures, no unseen, no angel, no judging hearts.
subtitle: Nuh says honestly what he is not

key.label: The people you look down on

then: Nuh told his people plainly that he was {idea}only a human messenger{/idea}. He did not hold Allah's treasures, know the unseen, or claim to be an angel. And he would not say of the believers they looked down on that {trap}Allah would give them no good{/trap}. Allah knows what is inside them.
now: At the bus stop you see a man in a stained jacket, mumbling, and something in you files him as worthless. In the office you quietly rank people by title. {idea}You do not see souls.{/idea} The one your eyes dismiss may be dearer to Allah than you.
old: I can tell what a person is worth from how they look and where they stand.
new: Only Allah knows what is inside a soul, so writing someone off would make me the wrongdoer.
try: Catch one quick judgment you make about a stranger today and replace it with a silent prayer for them.

title: Enough talking, bring the punishment then.
subtitle: Tired of argument, they dare the warning
then: After long years of Nuh's advice, his people gave their final word. {trap}You have argued with us long enough, and we still will not follow you.{/trap} They asked him to bring the punishment he warned of, hurrying Allah's anger on themselves rather than change.
now: Your doctor has warned you about your blood sugar three visits in a row. You roll your eyes and say "we all die of something." {idea}A dare can be a way of not listening.{/idea} Sometimes "bring it on" just means "I will not change."
old: Challenging a warning shows I am not afraid of it.
new: Daring the warning to come is often just a way to avoid changing.
try: Think of one warning you keep brushing off, about health, money, or faith. Write down one small step you could take.

title: The punishment is not mine to bring.
subtitle: Nuh points them away from himself to Allah
then: They had dared Nuh to bring the punishment. He did not boast or threaten back. {idea}Only Allah brings it, if He wills{/idea}, he said, and {trap}no one can escape Him{/trap}. The warner is only a messenger, not the one in control.
now: Someone mocks you: "So where is this Day you keep talking about?" You feel you need to prove it on the spot. {idea}You do not hold the timing.{/idea} You can only say what you know and leave the rest with Allah.
old: If I cannot prove the warning right now, I look foolish.
new: The outcome and its timing belong to Allah; I am only asked to speak honestly.
try: When someone challenges your faith today, answer briefly and calmly, without needing to win.

title: Good advice cannot help a heart that refuses it.
subtitle: Sincere counsel has limits, and all return to Him
then: Nuh admitted the limit of his own effort. {trap}My advice will not benefit you{/trap} if Allah's will is to leave you astray. Then he reminded them who they were dealing with: {idea}He is your Lord, and to Him you will return{/idea}, the One who owns how every matter ends.
now: You have sent your friend article after article about leaving a harmful habit. You rewrite the perfect message at 1 a.m. {idea}Advice is your part. Guidance is Allah's.{/idea} You can give your best and still not be the one who changes a heart.
old: If they do not change, I must not have said it well enough.
new: I give sincere advice; whether it benefits is in Allah's hands, and we all return to Him.
try: Make dua tonight for one person you have been trying to advise, instead of sending another message.

title: If I made it up, the sin is mine alone.
subtitle: A pause in Nuh's story to answer Makkah
then: In the middle of Nuh's story, Allah turns to the Prophet ﷺ. The disbelievers of Makkah said {trap}he made this up{/trap}. He is told to answer: if I invented it, the crime is mine alone. {idea}But I am innocent of what you do.{/idea} The one who knows Allah's punishment for lying about Him would not lie.
now: Someone in the comments says your faith is something you were just taught and never checked. You feel defensive. {idea}You answer for your own choices{/idea}, and so do they. That thought is calming, not cold.
old: I have to defend myself against every accusation or it will stick.
new: Each person carries their own deeds before Allah; I only need to be honest in mine.
try: Let one unfair comment about you go unanswered today, and check only that your own conduct is clean.

title: No one else will believe. Do not grieve.
subtitle: Allah lifts the weight off Nuh's shoulders

row.title: their choices
sub: as if they were his fault

then: Nuh's people had hurried Allah's punishment on themselves, and Nuh had called to his Lord that he was overcome. Then came the revelation: {idea}none of your people will believe except those who already have{/idea}. {reward}So do not be distressed by what they do.{/reward}
now: You have kept the family together for years: the calls, the peace-making, the hosting. Some relatives still turn away. {reward}You are allowed to stop carrying their choices.{/reward} Doing your part is not the same as owning their response.
old: If they do not respond, it is a failure I must keep grieving.
new: Once I have done my part, Allah Himself tells me not to be crushed by others' choices.
try: Name one person whose choices you keep blaming yourself for. Say: I did my part, the rest is with Allah.

title: Build the ship under Our eyes.
subtitle: Work done while Allah watches and teaches
then: Allah told Nuh to build the ship {reward}under Our eyes and with Our revelation{/reward}, meaning He would watch and teach him what to do. Nuh was also told not to plead for the wrongdoers anymore. {trap}Their drowning had been decided.{/trap}
now: You are on a long night shift, or patching code nobody will praise, or cooking for a family that barely says thanks. It feels unseen. {idea}It is under His eyes.{/idea} Nuh's planks were not glamorous either.
old: Work nobody notices does not really count.
new: Every plank I lay is seen by Allah, and He guides the work I do for Him.
try: Before one ordinary task today, say quietly: You see this, so help me do it well.

title: They laughed at a ship on dry land.
subtitle: Mockery while obeying, and Nuh's steady reply
then: Nuh kept building. {trap}Every time the chiefs of his people passed, they mocked him{/trap}, rejecting his warning that they would drown. He did not stop. He answered that if they laughed now, {idea}the laughter would one day turn back on them{/idea}.
now: Your coworkers smirk when you step out to pray. Your friends tease you for skipping the bar night or saving instead of spending. {idea}Keep building.{/idea} Mockery is loud today, but it does not decide how things end.
old: If people laugh at what I am doing, maybe I am the one who is wrong.
new: Mockery does not make obedience foolish; the end will show who was right.
try: The next time someone teases you for a good habit, smile, say nothing back, and carry on.

title: Soon you will know who is disgraced.
subtitle: Two outcomes, here and after

row.title: the final outcome
sub: who is honored, who is not

then: Nuh finished his answer to the mockers with {trap}a serious warning{/trap}. They would soon see who would be humiliated in this life and who would face a lasting punishment after it. {idea}The scene at the shipyard was not the end of the story.{/idea}
now: You scroll past a clip of someone being mocked for their faith, and you laugh along before you think. Or you are the one laughed at. {idea}Today's laughter is not the last word.{/idea} Ask which side of that warning your own habits are building toward.
old: What people think of me right now is what matters.
new: The real outcome comes later, and it is my conduct, not the crowd, that decides it.
try: Skip or report one video today that mocks someone's faith instead of sharing it.

title: After all those years, only a few came aboard.
subtitle: The flood begins and the ship is loaded
then: When Allah's command came, water burst from the face of the earth, even from places where fire is lit. Nuh was told to load pairs of each creature, his household, and the believers. {trap}His son and his wife were not among them{/trap}, for they did not believe. {idea}Only a few believed{/idea}, even after nine hundred and fifty years of calling.
now: You count followers, likes, attendance at the halaqa, and feel like a failure when the numbers are small. {idea}Nuh had a few after centuries{/idea}, and he was still a success in Allah's eyes. Faithfulness is not measured in crowds.
old: If only a few people respond, my effort was wasted.
new: Allah measures sincerity, not numbers; a few who truly believe were enough for Nuh's ship.
try: Thank one person who has stayed loyal to a good effort of yours, even if they are the only one.

title: In Allah's name it sails and in His name it stops.
subtitle: Beginning a journey with His name
then: As the believers boarded, Nuh told them the ship's {idea}sailing and anchoring were in the name of Allah{/idea}. Even while the wrongdoers were about to drown, he called his Lord {reward}Forgiving and Merciful{/reward}. Ibn Kathir notes this is why saying Allah's name at the start of affairs, and when boarding or riding, is encouraged.
now: You get into the car for the school run, start the laptop for a hard meeting, sit down for a job interview. You usually just go. {idea}Say His name first.{/idea} The start and the stop of your day are in His hands.
old: My plans and preparation are what carry me through.
new: Every start and every stop happens by Allah's name, so I begin with it.
try: Say Bismillah out loud each time you start the car or a trip today.

title: My son, come aboard with us.
subtitle: A father's last call across the waves
then: The ship moved through {trap}waves like mountains{/trap}, carried by Allah's protection. Nuh saw his son Yam, a disbeliever, standing apart. {idea}He called him one more time{/idea}: come aboard with us, do not be with the disbelievers.
now: Your teenager has stopped praying and closes the door when you knock. Your grown child no longer answers your texts about faith. {idea}Nuh still called.{/idea} Love keeps the invitation open, gently, until the very end.
old: Once my child has turned away, there is nothing left to say.
new: A loving parent keeps calling softly, right up to the last chance.
try: Send one warm, pressure-free message to a family member who has drifted away.

title: No mountain is high enough against Allah's decree.
subtitle: The son trusts a mountain instead of mercy
then: The son answered that {trap}he would climb a mountain and the water would not reach him{/trap}. He thought the flood could not cover the peaks. Nuh told him that on this day {reward}there is no protector from Allah's command except His mercy{/reward}. Then a wave came between them.
now: You have your own mountains: the savings buffer, the insurance policy, the connections, the clever exit plan. They are useful, but they are not where safety comes from. {reward}Mercy is the only real high ground.{/reward}
old: As long as I have a backup plan, I am safe.
new: My plans help, but only Allah's mercy truly protects me.
try: When you check your bank balance or plans today, add a short dua asking Allah for His mercy.

title: Earth, swallow. Sky, hold back. And it was done.
subtitle: The flood ends at one command
then: When the deniers had drowned, Allah {idea}commanded the earth to swallow its water and the sky to stop{/idea}. The water sank, the matter was settled, and the ship came to rest on Mount Judi. Mujahid said the other mountains rose proud that day but Judi humbled itself. {trap}It was said: away with the wrongdoing people.{/trap}
now: You are in the middle of your own flood: the divorce paperwork, the layoff, the long diagnosis. It feels endless. {idea}The One who started it can end it with a word.{/idea} Storms obey Him.
old: This hard season will go on forever.
new: Every flood ends when Allah says so, and He can settle my matter in a moment.
try: Write one hard thing you are going through on paper and make dua that Allah settles it with ease.

title: My Lord, my son is of my family.
subtitle: A grieving father brings his question to Allah
then: After the flood, Nuh called to his Lord about his son. Allah had promised to save his family, and {reward}Allah's promise is true{/reward}. So how had his son drowned? It was {idea}a question, asked with respect{/idea}, ending with: You are the most just of judges.
now: You are in the hospital corridor after the news, or at home after a loss that makes no sense. Questions burn inside you. {idea}Bring them to Allah{/idea}, in prayer, the way Nuh did: honest grief, with trust still in it.
old: Questioning what happened means my faith is weak.
new: I can bring my hardest questions to Allah, as long as I bring them with trust.
try: In your next sujood, tell Allah honestly about one loss that still hurts.

title: He is not of your family, his deeds were not good.
subtitle: Faith, not blood, makes the family Allah saves
then: Allah answered that the son {idea}was not among the family He promised to save{/idea}. The promise was for those of his family who believed. Ibn Abbas said he was truly Nuh's son but {trap}opposed him in deeds and intention{/trap}. Nuh was told not to ask for what he had no knowledge of.
now: You assume that because your parents were pious, or your family is known at the masjid, you are covered. {idea}No one inherits faith.{/idea} Your own deeds are what place you in the family Allah saves.
old: Coming from a good family keeps me safe.
new: Belonging to the believers is about my own deeds, not my family name.
try: Pick one good habit you have relied on your family for, like dua or Quran, and do it yourself today.

title: Forgive me, or I will be among the losers.
subtitle: Nuh accepts the answer and turns to repentance
then: A great prophet, just corrected by Allah. Nuh did not argue or justify. {idea}He sought refuge from asking what he had no knowledge of{/idea}, and said that unless Allah forgave him and had mercy on him, {reward}he would be among the losers{/reward}.
now: Your boss points out a mistake in the report, or your spouse tells you your words hurt. Your first reflex is to explain why you were right. {idea}Nuh just turned back.{/idea} A sincere "forgive me" is stronger than a clever defense.
old: When I am corrected, I need to explain my side.
new: When corrected, the noblest response is to accept it and ask for forgiveness.
try: Next time you are corrected today, say "you are right, I am sorry" before anything else.

title: Step down in peace, with blessings on you.
subtitle: A new beginning for Nuh and those after him
then: When the ship rested, Nuh was told to {reward}come down with peace and blessings{/reward}, on him and on nations from those with him. Muhammad bin Ka'b said every believing man and woman until the Day of Resurrection is included in that peace. {trap}Others would enjoy life for a time, then meet punishment.{/trap}
now: You moved to a new city, started over after a breakup, or walked out of the hospital after recovery. A new beginning. {reward}The same peace is offered to you{/reward}, if you step into it as a believer.
old: Peace and blessing were for prophets long ago, not for someone like me.
new: The peace given to Nuh reaches every believer after him, including me.
try: On your next fresh start, even a new week, begin it with a short prayer for peace and blessing.

title: You did not know this story. So be patient.
subtitle: Nuh's story told to strengthen the Prophet ﷺ
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ that this story was {idea}news of the unseen{/idea}; neither he nor his people knew it before, so no one could say he learned it from them. He is told to be patient with his people's rejection and harm. {reward}The good end is for those with taqwa.{/reward}
now: You are the only one at work who will not fudge the numbers. You are the sibling who keeps the peace while others gossip. It feels like losing. {reward}The story is not over.{/reward} Nuh's story is told so you keep going.
old: If doing right is costing me now, maybe it is not worth it.
new: Patience is worth it, because the final outcome belongs to the mindful.
try: Pick one right choice that has been costing you, and keep it one more day with the words: the end is for taqwa.

title: Their brother came with one message.
subtitle: Hud calls 'Ad to worship Allah alone
then: After Nuh, the surah turns to the people of 'Ad and {idea}their brother Hud{/idea}, one of their own. He told them to worship Allah alone. The idols they worshipped were {trap}names they had invented and called gods{/trap}.
now: Nobody around you bows to statues. But you might check your phone before you pray, or let a salary figure decide your mood. {trap}Some gods are just made-up importance.{/trap} Hud's call still applies: only One deserves that place.
old: Idol worship is something from the ancient past.
new: Anything I give Allah's place to is an invention, however modern it looks.
try: Notice the first thing you reach for when you wake up tomorrow, and make it a short dhikr instead.

title: He wanted nothing from them. Will you not think?
subtitle: Free advice is a sign of sincerity

row.title: who said it
sub: one of us, so ignore him

then: Hud told 'Ad he asked them {reward}no reward{/reward}; his reward was with the One who created him. Ibn Kathir explains the point: someone is calling you to {idea}what benefits your life here and after{/idea}, and wants nothing from you. Will you not reason?
now: The influencer sells you the course, the salesman needs his commission, the app wants your attention. Then a friend tells you something hard for your own good, and gets nothing out of it. {idea}That is the voice to listen to.{/idea}
old: Advice that is free is probably worth what I paid for it.
new: Advice from someone who wants nothing from me deserves my attention most.
try: Think of someone who once told you a hard truth for free. Thank them today.

title: Seek forgiveness and the sky opens.
subtitle: Repentance brings rain and added strength
then: 'Ad were a powerful people. Hud told them to {idea}seek forgiveness for the past and repent for the future{/idea}. Ibn Kathir notes that whoever does this, Allah makes provision and affairs easy for him. {reward}He would send them rain and add strength to their strength.{/reward} Do not turn away as criminals.
now: It is payday and the money is already gone. The project at work is stuck. You feel drained. {reward}Istighfar is not only for sins{/reward}; it opens doors you cannot open yourself.
old: Seeking forgiveness is only for when I have done something terrible.
new: Turning back to Allah brings ease and strength into my everyday life.
try: Say astaghfirullah slowly 30 times on your commute or before sleep tonight.

title: We will not leave our gods on your word.
subtitle: Calling it no proof to avoid changing
then: 'Ad answered Hud: {trap}you have brought us no clear proof{/trap}, and we will not leave our gods just because you say so. They asked how his mere words could be enough. Yet Ibn Kathir notes the idols they defended could not hear, see, help, or harm.
now: You know the habit is hurting you: the late-night scrolling, the gossip, the loan you keep rolling over. Someone warns you and you say, "Prove it." {idea}Sometimes asking for proof is a way to keep holding on.{/idea}
old: I will change when someone gives me enough proof.
new: Often I already know; asking for more proof can be a way to avoid letting go.
try: Name one thing you keep asking for "more proof" about before changing. Take one step anyway.

title: Our gods have struck you with madness.
subtitle: Attacking the messenger instead of the message
then: 'Ad said the only explanation was that {trap}one of their gods had afflicted Hud with madness{/trap}, because he spoke against them. Hud did not shrink back. {idea}He called Allah to witness, and them too{/idea}, that he was free of everything they set up beside Allah.
now: You start praying at work or quit drinking, and friends say, "What happened to you? You have gone strange." {idea}A label is not an argument.{/idea} Hud stood calm and clear when he was called mad.
old: If people say I have gone strange, I should go back to how I was.
new: Being called strange for following the truth says nothing about the truth.
try: If someone teases you for a faith choice today, answer once, kindly and clearly, without apologizing for it.

title: Plot against me, all of you, and do not wait.
subtitle: One man challenges a whole nation and its idols
then: Hud turned the threat around. If your gods are real, {trap}plot against me, all of you, you and your gods{/trap}, and give me no respite, not even the blink of an eye. {idea}He knew their idols could do nothing.{/idea}
now: You are scared to speak up in the meeting, to refuse the bribe, to stop laughing at the cruel joke. The crowd feels huge. {idea}Their power is smaller than it looks.{/idea} The fear you feel was always weaker than the One you trust.
old: If everyone is against me, I cannot stand.
new: When I stand with Allah, the crowd's power over me is far smaller than it seems.
try: Say no to one small thing today you only went along with out of fear of others.

title: Every creature's forelock is in His hand.
subtitle: Trust in Allah, who controls every living thing
then: Hud gave the reason for his calm: {idea}I have relied on Allah, my Lord and your Lord.{/idea} There is no moving creature except that He holds it by the forelock. Ibn Kathir says every creature is under His power, and {reward}He is just, never unjust in His ruling{/reward}.
now: The landlord, the immigration officer, the boss who controls your contract. They seem to hold your future. {idea}Each of them is held by Allah.{/idea} You can be respectful and still not be afraid.
old: The people with power over me decide what happens to me.
new: Every person with power is in Allah's grip, so my trust goes to Him.
try: Before facing someone who intimidates you, say quietly: my Lord holds them too.

title: Turn away if you want; you will not harm Him.
subtitle: The message delivered, the outcome with Allah
then: Hud told 'Ad that if they turned away, {idea}he had delivered what he was sent with{/idea}. Allah would bring another people to replace them. Their disbelief {trap}would not harm Allah at all, only themselves{/trap}. He watches over every word and deed.
now: You skip the prayer and somehow feel you are hurting religion, or Allah. You are not. {trap}The one who loses is you{/trap}: the calm, the light, the help that prayer brings. He is the Guardian of all things; your worship is for your own good.
old: When I neglect my worship, I am letting Allah down.
new: Allah needs nothing from me; neglecting worship only harms me.
try: Pray your next salah with the thought: this is for me, not for Him.

title: Saved by mercy from a harsh punishment.
subtitle: Hud and the believers are rescued
then: When Allah's command came, the {trap}barren wind{/trap} destroyed the deniers among 'Ad. Ibn Kathir says Allah's mercy and kindness {reward}saved Hud and those who believed with him{/reward} from that terrible punishment.
now: You got through the year: the car accident that could have been worse, the test result that came back clear. You might credit your caution or luck. {reward}It was mercy.{/reward} Even the believers were saved by mercy, not by merit.
old: I got through because I was careful and did things right.
new: Every rescue in my life is a mercy from Allah, not my own achievement.
try: Recall one close call you survived and say alhamdulillah for it by name.

title: They followed every proud tyrant instead.
subtitle: Whom 'Ad chose to obey
then: This was 'Ad. They {trap}rejected their Lord's signs and disobeyed His messengers{/trap}. Ibn Kathir explains that rejecting one prophet is rejecting all of them. They left their rightly guided messenger and {trap}followed every proud, stubborn tyrant{/trap}.
now: Think about whose voice you follow. The loud man at work who mocks rules, the friend who always pushes the reckless plan, the creator you binge every night. {idea}Who you obey shapes who you become.{/idea}
old: I just go along with the strong personalities around me.
new: Whose lead I follow is a choice, and it decides where I end up.
try: List the three voices that influence your choices most. Ask if each points you toward Allah.

title: Remembered with a curse, here and on the Day.
subtitle: How a powerful nation's story ends
then: The story of 'Ad closes soberly. Ibn Kathir says they are {trap}followed by a curse from Allah and the believers whenever they are mentioned{/trap}, and a call will be made against them on the Day of Resurrection. {idea}They denied their Lord.{/idea}
now: You think about how you will be remembered: at your job, in your family, at your funeral. Not by your car or your title. {idea}By how you answered the truth when it came to you.{/idea} That is still in your hands today.
old: My legacy is what I build and achieve.
new: What lasts is how I answered Allah's call, and that is mine to shape now.
try: Write one sentence you hope people say about you after you die, and do one thing today that fits it.

title: The One who built you is near and answers.
subtitle: Salih's first words to a prosperous people

row.title: near, responsive
sub: He hears the one who calls

then: Thamud lived after the people of 'Ad, in cities carved from rock between Tabuk and Madinah. Allah sent them one of their own, Salih. He reminded them that {reward}the land they treasured was a gift{/reward}, and told them to {idea}ask forgiveness for the past and turn to Allah for the future{/idea}.
now: You have a decent flat, a job, a car that starts. It all feels like something you built. Then one night something goes wrong and you are not sure He is listening. {idea}He is near, and He answers.{/idea} The door back is two steps: sorry for yesterday, a new direction for tomorrow.
old: What I have, I earned, and Allah feels far away.
new: He made me, He settled me where I am, and He is close enough to answer tonight.
try: Tonight, ask forgiveness for one specific thing, then name one small change for tomorrow.

title: We had such hopes for you, until you said this.
subtitle: When people liked you until you spoke the truth
then: Salih had a good name among his people. They said they had placed their hopes in his strong mind. Once he called them to worship Allah alone, {trap}their respect turned into suspicion{/trap}. Their only argument was {trap}this is what our fathers worshipped{/trap}.
now: You were the golden child of the family. Then you started praying, or stopped joining in something everyone does. Now the aunties say you have changed, and not in a good way. {idea}Their disappointment is not proof you are wrong.{/idea}
old: If the people who loved me now doubt me, I must be making a mistake.
new: Losing people's approval for the truth is a cost, not a verdict.
try: Think of one habit you keep only because the family always did it. Ask honestly if it is right.

title: Who would protect me from Allah if I gave in?
subtitle: Why Salih could not simply go quiet
then: His people wanted Salih to drop his message and go back to being their hope. He answered with a question. He was sure of what Allah gave him. {trap}If he abandoned it to please them, who could help him against Allah?{/trap} {idea}Their approval would only add to his loss.{/idea}
now: A colleague asks you to sign off on numbers you know are wrong. "Everyone does it, don't be difficult." Saying yes would make the meeting easier. {trap}It would not make you safer.{/trap} The people pushing you cannot carry what you sign.
old: Going along keeps me safe with the people around me.
new: The people pressing me to drop what is right cannot protect me from its cost.
try: Next time you feel pressure to bend, ask silently: will they stand with me before Allah?

title: A sign walking among them, with one simple rule.
subtitle: The she-camel of Allah and a test of restraint
then: Salih pointed to a she-camel and called it the camel of Allah, a sign for them. The rule was small: {idea}let her graze freely in Allah's land{/idea}. {trap}Harming her would bring a punishment that was close.{/trap}
now: Some tests do not ask you to do anything big. Just leave alone what is not yours. The colleague's idea. The neighbour's parking spot. The thing in the shop you could slip into your bag. {idea}Restraint is the whole test.{/idea}
old: Tests are about big deeds I have to perform.
new: Sometimes the test is simply to keep my hands off what Allah said to leave alone.
try: Today, notice one thing you are tempted to take or meddle with, and leave it.

title: Three days left, and the promise would not fail.
subtitle: The window after the line was crossed
then: They did exactly what they were told not to do. {trap}They hamstrung the camel.{/trap} Salih told them to enjoy their homes for three days. {idea}It was a promise that would not be belied.{/idea}
now: You ignored the doctor's warning, and the next morning you felt fine. Maybe nothing will happen. The days after a wrong can feel normal. {idea}Quiet is not the same as safe.{/idea} That gap is time to turn back.
old: If nothing bad happened right away, the warning was not serious.
new: A delay after a warning is a window, not a pardon.
try: Think of a warning you have been brushing off. Take one step on it today.

title: Saved by mercy, and spared the shame of that day.
subtitle: Salih and the believers when the command came
then: When the three days ended, Allah's command came. {reward}Salih and those who believed with him were saved by mercy from Allah{/reward}, and kept from {trap}the disgrace of that day{/trap}. The verse ends by reminding the Prophet ﷺ that his Lord is the Strong, the Mighty.
now: You are the only one at work who will not join the shady side deal. You feel small and outnumbered. {idea}Being outnumbered is not the same as being weak.{/idea} The strength in this story belonged to Allah, not to the crowd.
old: The few who do right are the ones who lose.
new: Rescue comes from His mercy, and strength is His, not the crowd's.
try: Thank Allah today for one time you were kept from something shameful.

title: One cry, and the homes they trusted held them still.
subtitle: How the wrongdoers of Thamud were taken
then: Thamud trusted their homes carved into rock. {trap}The cry came and they lay fallen in those same homes.{/trap} The verse calls them {trap}those who wronged{/trap}. Their walls did nothing for them.
now: You lock the door, check the alarm, top up the savings. That care is good. But some nights you feel nothing can touch you behind it. {idea}No wall replaces being right with Allah.{/idea}
old: Strong walls and good security keep me safe.
new: My real safety is how I stand with Allah, not the walls around me.
try: Before you sleep tonight, make a short du'a for protection instead of only checking the locks.

title: As if they had never lived there at all.
subtitle: What remains of a prosperity that denied its Lord
then: After the cry, Thamud's busy cities looked {trap}as if no one had ever prospered there{/trap}. The verse names the cause plainly: {trap}they denied their Lord{/trap}. Their story closes with the words: away with Thamud.
now: You scroll past an old photo of a crowded shop that is now boarded up. Busy places empty out. Lives that seemed so full get forgotten. {idea}What lasts is what you did with Allah in mind.{/idea}
old: What I am building now will always be here.
new: All of it can vanish as if it never was. Only my standing with my Lord stays.
try: Pick one thing you are building this week and give it a purpose that pleases Allah.

title: He greeted them with peace and hurried to feed them.
subtitle: Ibrahim, the strangers, and the roasted calf
then: Angels came to Ibrahim with good news, looking like young men. They said peace, and {idea}he answered with an even better greeting of peace{/idea}. Then {reward}he wasted no time and brought them a roasted calf{/reward}. Ibn Kathir notes the verse teaches many manners of hosting guests.
now: Someone you barely know turns up at the door, or a new colleague sits alone at lunch. Your first thought is how busy you are. {idea}Greet them warmly, and offer something good without making them wait.{/idea}
old: I will be generous once I know who someone is.
new: Warmth first, quickly, with the best I have. That is how Ibrahim met strangers.
try: Offer a drink or snack to the next person who visits you, before they have to ask.

title: Their hands did not reach for the food.
subtitle: Ibrahim's unease, and the guests' calming words

row.title: fear not
sub: sent to the people of Lut

then: Ibrahim set the food down, but {trap}their hands did not reach for it{/trap}. Angels do not eat, and a guest refusing food felt strange and worrying. They reassured him: {idea}do not fear, we were sent to the people of Lut{/idea}.
now: A message from your manager: "Can we talk tomorrow?" You spend the night sure you are being let go. It turns out to be a new project. {idea}Not every strange sign means harm is coming for you.{/idea}
old: When something feels off, the worst must be coming for me.
new: Even a prophet felt fear at the unknown, and the answer was: fear not.
try: Next time worry spikes, say a short du'a and wait for the facts before deciding the worst.

title: She laughed, then heard of a son and grandson.
subtitle: Sarah standing by, and news she never expected

key.label: What she thought her future held

then: Sarah stood nearby serving the guests. When she heard they were sent against the people of Lut, who had spread great corruption, she laughed. Ibn Kathir says {reward}she was then given news of a son, Ishaq, after she had given up hope{/reward}, and {reward}after him a grandson, Ya'qub{/reward}.
now: You stopped talking about it years ago. The job, the child, the healing, the reunion. You filed it under "not for me." {idea}Allah's gifts do not run on your timeline.{/idea}
old: Some doors closed for good a long time ago.
new: Allah can open a door I stopped knocking on, and give more than I asked.
try: Make du'a tonight for one thing you quietly stopped asking for.

title: Me? A mother, now, at my age?
subtitle: Sarah's honest astonishment at the news

key.label: Her measure of what is possible

then: Sarah reacted the way women of her time showed amazement. {idea}She was old, her husband was very old, and a child seemed impossible.{/idea} She said out loud that this was a strange thing. Her surprise was honest, not defiant.
now: Someone tells you there is still a chance: the exam you failed twice, the loan, the reconciliation. You laugh and list every reason it cannot happen. {idea}Your list is real. It is just not the last word.{/idea}
old: Looking at the facts, this simply cannot happen to me.
new: My facts are real, but they do not limit what Allah can do.
try: Write down one "impossible" hope. Next to it write: Allah is able.

title: Why wonder at Allah's command? Mercy is on this house.
subtitle: The angels' reply to Sarah

row.title: Allah's command
sub: He says Be, and it is

then: The angels told Sarah not to be amazed at Allah's command. {idea}When He wants something, He says Be and it is{/idea}, even for an old couple. Then they prayed for {reward}Allah's mercy and blessings on the household of Ibrahim{/reward}.
now: Good news finally comes and you cannot quite believe it. You keep waiting for the catch. {idea}Let shock turn into thanks.{/idea} A blessed home is not one with no hardship. It is one Allah's mercy rests on.
old: When something good finally happens, I wait for it to fall apart.
new: Allah's command is easy for Him. The right response to His gift is praise.
try: Say alhamdulillah out loud for one good thing in your home today.

title: His fear gone, he began pleading for others.
subtitle: Ibrahim argues for the people of Lut

key.label: What he did with good news

then: Once Ibrahim's fear of the guests was gone and the good news reached him, he did not just relax. Ibn Kathir reports from Sa'id bin Jubayr that {idea}he asked the angels again and again{/idea}: would you destroy a town with three hundred believers, forty, five, one? Then he said, Lut is there. {reward}They answered that they would save Lut and his family{/reward}, except his wife.
now: Your own result comes back fine. The scan is clear, the job is safe. That same evening you hear a friend is in trouble. {idea}The first thing you do with relief can be to stand up for someone else.{/idea}
old: Once my own problem is solved, I can stop worrying.
new: When my fear lifts, I have room to plead for others.
try: Make du'a today, by name, for someone going through what you were spared.

title: Gentle, quick to grieve, always turning back.
subtitle: Allah's praise of Ibrahim's character
then: Right after Ibrahim pleaded for the people of Lut, Allah praised him. Ibn Kathir calls it {reward}a commendation for beautiful qualities{/reward}: {idea}forbearing, humble in calling on Allah, and always turning back to Him{/idea}. His plea came from mercy, not stubbornness.
now: Someone in the family group chat says something cruel about a relative who messed up. You feel the pull to pile on. {idea}You can be the one who stays patient, feels for them, and quietly prays.{/idea} That softness is a strength.
old: Feeling for people who did wrong makes me weak.
new: A heart that grieves for others and keeps turning to Allah is one He praises.
try: Next time you hear someone being mocked for their faults, stay silent and make a short du'a for them.

title: Leave this, Ibrahim. The decision has already come.
subtitle: When pleading reaches a settled decree
then: Ibrahim's plea was praised, but there was a limit. The angels told him to leave it. {idea}The command of his Lord had been settled.{/idea} For a people who would not stop their wrongdoing, {trap}the punishment could not be turned back{/trap}.
now: You have done everything for someone: talked, warned, prayed, paid. They still chose the path that hurt them. You lie awake replaying it. {idea}You did your part. The outcome was never yours to hold.{/idea}
old: If I had just tried harder, I could have changed what happened.
new: I plead with all my heart, then leave the decision to Allah.
try: Think of one outcome you keep trying to control. Say: I have done my part, the rest is Yours.

title: Guests arrived, and Lut knew it would be a hard day.
subtitle: Lut's distress at protecting his guests
then: The angels left Ibrahim and came to Lut in the form of young men. He did not know who they were. {trap}He feared his people would harm them{/trap}, so he took them in, knowing he would have to defend them. Ibn 'Abbas explained his words as {idea}a severe test for him{/idea}.
now: A new kid at school is being picked on, or a junior colleague is being set up to take the blame. Stepping in means trouble for you. {idea}Sometimes doing right means walking into a hard day on purpose.{/idea}
old: If helping someone will cost me, it is not my problem.
new: A hard day taken on to protect someone is a test worth meeting.
try: Notice one person around you who is exposed or alone today, and stand next to them.

title: Is there not one sensible man among you?
subtitle: Lut pleads with a crowd at his door

row.title: Lut
sub: like a father to his nation

then: His people came rushing, a people {trap}long used to doing evil{/trap}. Lut pointed them to the women of the nation in lawful marriage. Mujahid said these were not his own daughters but the women of his people, since {idea}a prophet is like a father to his nation{/idea}. He asked them to fear Allah and not shame him with his guests.
now: A group chat starts sharing something cruel, and everyone sends laughing emojis. You type "guys, come on" and wait. {idea}You are hoping one person will be the sensible one.{/idea} Be that person when someone else asks.
old: When everyone is doing it, one voice against it is pointless.
new: A single right-minded person in a crowd can matter. I can be that one.
try: The next time a group heads somewhere wrong, be the first to quietly back the person saying stop.

title: You know what we want. Why keep talking?
subtitle: A people who refused the lawful
then: Lut's people rejected the lawful path outright. {trap}They told him he already knew what they wanted{/trap}, so what was the point of talking? Ibn Kathir explains they meant {trap}there was no need for him to continue speaking{/trap}.
now: You catch yourself saying "I know, I know" before a parent or friend has even finished. Your mind is already made up about what you want. {idea}Closing the conversation early is often how a heart closes too.{/idea}
old: I already know what I want, so advice is just noise.
new: When I shut down the person warning me, that is the moment to listen hardest.
try: Next time you want to say "I know," let the other person finish first.

title: If only I had strength, or a strong support.
subtitle: Lut alone at his door
then: Lut stood at the door with no clan behind him. He wished for {idea}the strength to stop them, or a strong support to turn to{/idea}. Ibn Kathir reports the Prophet ﷺ said: may Allah have mercy on Lut, {reward}he was turning to a strong support{/reward}, meaning Allah.
now: You are the one standing up to a bully, a boss, a wrong at home, and you have no backup. Nobody is replying to your messages. {reward}Feeling alone does not mean you are alone.{/reward}
old: Without people behind me, I have no protection.
new: When no one else stands behind me, Allah is the strong support I can lean on.
try: When you feel unbacked today, say quietly: hasbiyallah, Allah is enough for me.

title: They will not reach you. Leave by night, do not look back.
subtitle: The angels reveal themselves to Lut
then: Now the guests told Lut who they were: {reward}messengers of his Lord, and his people would not reach him{/reward}. He was to leave in the last part of the night with his family and {idea}not turn back toward the noise{/idea}. His wife would not be saved with them. {idea}The appointed time was the morning, and it was near.{/idea}
now: You finally decide to leave a habit, a toxic friendship, a job that was eating your faith. Then the old life calls: one more look, one more message. {idea}Leaving well means not turning back to watch.{/idea}
old: I can leave it behind and still keep looking back at it.
new: When Allah opens a way out, I walk it and do not look back.
try: Unfollow, mute, or delete one thing that keeps pulling you back to what you left.

title: The town was turned upside down at sunrise.
subtitle: When the command came to the people of Lut
then: At sunrise, Allah's command came. {trap}The town was turned upside down{/trap} and {trap}stones of hardened clay fell in succession{/trap}. Lut and his family had left in the night as instructed. A people who had refused every warning were taken.
now: Some things around you feel so normal, so fixed, that nobody questions them anymore. A habit at work, a way of talking, something you scroll past every day. {idea}What looks permanent can be overturned in one morning.{/idea} The question is what your own life is built on.
old: The way things are around me is how they will always be.
new: Only what is built on obeying Allah stays standing.
try: Look at one normal habit in your day and ask: would I want this as my last morning?

title: Marked by your Lord, and never far from wrongdoers.
subtitle: A warning that reaches past one town
then: The stones were {trap}marked from Allah{/trap}, each meant for its target. The verse closes with a line for everyone after: {idea}this is never far from those who do wrong{/idea}. Ibn Kathir explains that the same vengeance is not far from similar wrongdoers.
now: It is easy to read an old story and think of other people. The real question is closer. The lie you told yesterday, the cruelty you excused, the thing you keep doing in private. {idea}The warning is for you, so you can turn back while you can.{/idea}
old: Stories of punishment are about other people far away.
new: The warning sits close to any wrong, including mine. That is a mercy: I can still turn.
try: Name one wrong you keep repeating, and ask Allah's forgiveness for it before you sleep.

title: You are doing well. So why cheat the scale?
subtitle: Shu'ayb's call to a prosperous trading people

row.title: proof I'm fine
sub: so a little cheating is ok

then: Madyan was an Arab tribe between the Hijaz and Sham. Allah sent them Shu'ayb, one of their noblest. He called them to worship Allah alone and {trap}stop cheating in weights and measures{/trap}. He told them, {reward}I see you prospering{/reward}, and he feared they would lose it and face a Day that surrounds everyone.
now: The business is doing fine. Still, you round the hours up on the invoice. You sell the used phone without mentioning the cracked battery. {trap}A small cut on the scale.{/trap} You do not even need it.
old: I am doing well, so a little edge here and there does not matter.
new: My prosperity is a reason for honesty, not an excuse to shortchange.
try: Check one bill, invoice, or sale this week and make sure it is exactly fair.

title: Give people their full due, giving and receiving.
subtitle: Justice in every transaction
then: Shu'ayb told them to give {idea}just measure whether they were giving or receiving{/idea}, and not to reduce what was owed to people. Ibn Kathir notes they also {trap}robbed travellers on the roads{/trap}, which was the corruption in the land he forbade.
now: You pay the cleaner late and a little less than agreed. You quietly keep the extra change. You underrate a colleague's work in the review so yours looks better. {idea}People's due is not only money.{/idea}
old: Fairness is about not stealing outright.
new: Fairness means giving everyone their full due, in every exchange, both ways.
try: Pay one person you owe today, in full and on time, or give one colleague credit they earned.

title: What is left after honesty is better for you.
subtitle: Clean profit versus wrongful gain
then: Ibn Jarir explains that {reward}the profit left after giving people their rights is better{/reward} than taking their wealth wrongfully. Ibn Kathir links it to the verse that the bad and the good are not equal, even if the bad is plentiful. Shu'ayb added he was not their guardian: {idea}do this for Allah, not to be seen{/idea}.
now: Payday comes and it is smaller than your friend's, who cuts corners. You feel like the fool for being honest. {reward}The smaller, clean amount carries blessing.{/reward} And nobody is checking but Allah.
old: Honest money is less, so honesty is a loss.
new: What remains lawful from Allah is worth more than a bigger pile gained wrongly.
try: Look at your next payment and thank Allah that it is clean, whatever the size.

title: Does your prayer tell us how to spend our money?
subtitle: Mocking the idea that prayer reaches business
then: Shu'ayb had told Madyan to stop cheating in weights and measures. They mocked him: does {trap}your prayer{/trap} order us to leave our fathers' gods, or to stop doing what we like with our wealth? Ibn Abbas and others said that calling him {trap}the forbearing, the right-minded{/trap} was sarcasm.
now: You pray on time, then fudge the timesheet or overcharge a customer who will never notice. A colleague says, "Religion has nothing to do with business." {idea}Shu'ayb's people said the same.{/idea} Real prayer walks with you into the shop and the spreadsheet.
old: My prayer is between me and Allah; how I handle money is a separate matter.
new: Prayer is meant to shape how I earn and spend, not stay on the prayer mat.
try: Check one transaction or bill you handle today and make sure it is fully fair.

title: I only want to fix things, as much as I can.
subtitle: Shu'ayb practices what he asks of others

row.title: no double standard
sub: I do not do what I forbid

row.title: reform
sub: as far as I am able

then: Shu'ayb answered calmly. He had clear guidance and good provision from his Lord. Qatadah explained his words: {idea}I do not forbid you something while doing it myself.{/idea} He only wanted reform as far as he could, and said {reward}my success is only through Allah{/reward}.
now: You tell your kids to put the phone away at dinner while yours is in your hand. You ask your team to be on time and you walk in late. {idea}Advice lands when your life matches it.{/idea} Then leave the result to Allah.
old: I can tell others what is right even if I do not do it myself.
new: I give advice best by living it, and I rely on Allah for the result.
try: Pick one thing you often tell others to do, and do it yourself today first.

title: Do not let your dislike of me ruin you.
subtitle: Spite against the messenger as a trap

row.title: the grudge
sub: I will not let him be right

then: Shu'ayb warned his people: {trap}do not let your hatred of me push you to persist{/trap} in corruption. Otherwise you may meet what struck the peoples of Nuh, Hud and Salih. And Lut's people were not far off. Qatadah said they had only been destroyed yesterday, as it were.
now: Your sister gives you good advice about your marriage, but because it is her, you do the opposite. Your coworker is right about the plan, but you dislike him. {trap}Spite can make you reject what helps you.{/trap}
old: I cannot take advice from someone I do not like.
new: My dislike of a person should never push me away from a truth they carry.
try: Think of advice you dismissed because of who said it. Take one honest look at it today.

title: My Lord is Merciful and Loving.
subtitle: After the warning, the door to return

row.title: Al-Wadud
sub: who loves the one who returns

then: Right after warning of past nations, Shu'ayb opened the door. {idea}Ask your Lord's forgiveness for past sins and repent for what is ahead.{/idea} Then he described Allah: {reward}Merciful and Loving{/reward} toward those who repent.
now: You slipped back into the same habit again last night and feel too ashamed to pray. You think He must be tired of you. {reward}He is Loving to the one who returns.{/reward} The warning was never meant to shut the door.
old: After so many relapses, Allah must be done with me.
new: Allah is Merciful and Loving, and returning to Him is always welcome.
try: Make wudu and pray two rakat tonight, asking forgiveness for one specific thing.

title: If not for your clan, we would have stoned you.
subtitle: Truth dismissed because its speaker seems weak

row.title: your clan
sub: the only reason we hold back

then: Ath-Thawri said Shu'ayb was called {idea}the orator of the prophets{/idea}, yet his people said they did not understand much of what he said. They saw him as weak, only one man. {trap}Only respect for his clan stopped them from stoning him.{/trap}
now: In the family WhatsApp group, the quiet cousin with no degree says something wise and nobody replies. The same idea from the rich uncle gets ten hearts. {idea}Truth does not depend on who backs the speaker.{/idea}
old: I listen to people based on how important they are.
new: A true word deserves attention whoever says it and whoever stands behind them.
try: Reply warmly today to someone whose comment usually gets ignored.

title: You fear my clan more than you fear Allah?
subtitle: Throwing Allah behind your back
then: Shu'ayb asked: {trap}is my clan more weighty to you than Allah?{/trap} You would leave me alone out of regard for my tribe, but not out of awe of the Lord. They had {trap}thrown Him behind their backs{/trap}. But {idea}my Lord surrounds all that you do{/idea}.
now: You would never shout at your mother in front of guests, but alone you do. You drive the speed limit only near the camera. {idea}You are never alone with Him.{/idea} The question is whose gaze really holds you back.
old: What really stops me is what people will think.
new: Allah sees everything I do, and His awareness should matter more than anyone's.
try: Notice one thing you do only when no one is watching, and do it as if He is watching, because He is.

title: Do your work, I am doing mine. Wait and see.
subtitle: Parting words when the arguing is over
then: When Shu'ayb gave up hope of their response, he said: {trap}act according to your way, and I will act according to mine{/trap}. Ibn Kathir calls this a severe threat. Soon they would know who would be disgraced and who was lying. {idea}Wait, and I will wait with you.{/idea}
now: The argument in the comment thread has gone 40 replies. The family debate about honesty in business keeps circling. {idea}At some point you stop arguing and just keep doing right.{/idea} Your conduct will speak when words do not.
old: I need to keep arguing until the other side admits I am right.
new: After I have spoken clearly, I can stop arguing and let my conduct and time speak.
try: Leave one ongoing argument today with a calm last line and get on with doing good.

title: A single cry, and they lay still in their homes.
subtitle: Shu'ayb saved, the wrongdoers seized
then: Allah saved Shu'ayb and the believers {reward}by mercy from Him{/reward}. The wrongdoers were seized by {trap}a mighty cry{/trap} and lay lifeless in their homes. Ibn Kathir notes other surahs mention a quake and a shadow cloud; here the cry is mentioned because of how disrespectfully they spoke to their prophet.
now: Think of how you talk to the people Allah sent into your life to guide you: parents, teachers, the imam. {idea}How you speak matters to Allah.{/idea} Respect in words is part of faith.
old: Harsh words are just words; they do not count for much.
new: The way I speak to those who guide me is weighed by Allah.
try: Speak to a parent or teacher today with deliberate gentleness, even if you disagree.

title: As if they had never lived there at all.
subtitle: Madyan gone, like its neighbor Thamud

row.title: a passing stay
sub: gone as if it never was

then: After the cry, Madyan's homes stood {trap}as if no one had ever prospered in them{/trap}. They went away just as Thamud had. Ibn Kathir says Thamud were their neighbors, {idea}similar in disbelief and in highway robbery{/idea}.
now: You drive past the shop that was always busy and now has a for-lease sign. The house you grew up in has strangers in it. {idea}Every place we fill is a passing stay.{/idea} What will you have sent ahead when you leave yours?
old: My home, business, and wealth feel permanent.
