new: Everything I have built here is temporary; only what I send ahead remains.
try: Give something today from what you have, money, food, or time, as something sent ahead.

title: Musa came with signs and clear authority.
subtitle: The last story in the surah's series

row.title: clear authority
sub: an argument they could not answer

row.title: enough proof
sub: if only we had seen more

then: After Nuh, Hud, Salih, Lut and Shu'ayb, the surah briefly tells of Musa. Allah sent him {idea}with His signs and clear proofs{/idea} to Fir'awn, king of the Copts, and his chiefs. {trap}The proof was not lacking.{/trap}
now: You tell yourself you would pray more if you only felt a sign, a dream, a clear moment. Yet the signs are already there: the breath you took, the morning you woke to. {idea}The proof is not missing. Attention is.{/idea}
old: If I saw a clear sign, I would finally change.
new: Allah has already sent clear signs; what I need is the will to respond.
try: Write down three signs of Allah you saw today without looking for anything special.

title: They followed Fir'awn, and he was no guide.
subtitle: Following the powerful over the proof
then: Musa came to Fir'awn and his chiefs, {trap}but they followed Fir'awn's command{/trap}, his path and methods of transgression. Ibn Kathir says there was {trap}no right guidance in it{/trap}, only ignorance, misguidance and stubbornness.
now: Your team lead tells you to hide a defect from the client, and everyone goes along because he signs the reviews. {idea}Rank is not the same as right.{/idea} You can be respectful and still refuse to follow wrong.
old: If the person in charge says so, it is not my responsibility.
new: Power does not make a command right, and I answer for whom I follow.
try: If you are asked to do something unfair today, politely ask once: is there an honest way to do this?

title: The leader walks ahead, and they follow him in.
subtitle: Followers end where their leader ends

row.title: just this life
sub: it is only work, only habit

then: Ibn Kathir says that {trap}just as they followed Fir'awn in this life, he will lead them on the Day of Resurrection{/trap}. He will walk ahead of his people into the Fire. Those who lead others into wrong carry a heavy share. {idea}Following is never neutral.{/idea}
now: Your feed is shaped by the voices you follow. Your habits are shaped by the friends you copy. {idea}Every follow is a direction.{/idea} Choose leaders you would be glad to walk behind on the Day.
old: Who I follow online or in life is a small, harmless choice.
new: The ones I follow are walking me somewhere, in this life and the next.
try: Unfollow one account that pulls you away from Allah, and follow one that pulls you closer.

title: A curse here and on the Day, a wretched gift.
subtitle: What followers of Fir'awn received
then: Fir'awn's followers were {trap}pursued by a curse in this world and on the Day of Resurrection{/trap}. Mujahid said another curse is added on that Day, so there are two. Ibn Abbas called it {trap}the curse of this life and the next{/trap}, the evil gift they were given.
now: You stayed quiet about the wrong at work to keep your bonus. You laughed along to keep your place in the group. {idea}Ask what that loyalty is really paying you.{/idea} The reward of following wrong is never what it promises.
old: Going along with the powerful pays off.
new: Whatever following wrong seems to give, its real gift is loss, here and after.
try: Think of one place where you go along with wrong to keep a benefit. Take one small step out.

title: Some towns still stand, some were mown down.
subtitle: Looking back at the ruins as a lesson
then: After the stories of the prophets and their nations, Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ these are {idea}news of the towns We relate to you{/idea}. Of them, some still stand, and {trap}some have been reaped, totally destroyed{/trap}, like a harvested field.
now: You watch a documentary about an ancient city in ruins, then switch to the next show. Or you walk past a closed-down factory that once employed half the town. {idea}Pause on it.{/idea} Every ruin is a question about how its people lived.
old: Stories of destroyed nations are just history.
new: These stories are told so I look at my own life while there is still time.
try: Next time you see ruins or an abandoned building, ask yourself one honest question about your own habits.

title: We did not wrong them; they wronged themselves.
subtitle: False gods added nothing but loss
then: Allah says {idea}We did not wrong them{/idea} when We destroyed them; {trap}they wronged themselves{/trap} by rejecting their messengers. When the command came, their idols could not help or save them. Mujahid and Qatadah said those gods only added loss.
now: You stayed up gaming instead of studying, then blamed the exam. You spent on credit, then blamed the bank. {idea}Some wounds are self-inflicted.{/idea} Seeing that is not shame; it is the start of change.
old: When things go badly, it is usually someone else's fault.
new: Allah wrongs no one; much of my harm comes from my own choices, which I can change.
try: Name one problem you keep blaming on others and write one thing you did that fed it.

title: Respite is long, but the seizing is sure.
subtitle: Delay is not escape
then: This is how Allah seizes towns that do wrong, and {trap}His seizing is painful and severe{/trap}. The Prophet ﷺ said Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer until, when He seizes him, he cannot escape, and then he recited this verse. {idea}What He did to them, He does to any like them.{/idea}
now: You have been cutting corners for months and nothing has happened. No audit, no consequence. It starts to feel safe. {idea}Respite is not approval.{/idea} It is time given to turn back while turning back is still possible.
old: If nothing bad has happened yet, what I am doing must be fine.
new: Delay is a mercy and a warning, not a sign that I got away with it.
try: Stop one small wrong today that you have been getting away with.

title: A Day everyone is gathered and everyone sees.
subtitle: The ruins point to a bigger gathering

row.title: a sign
sub: for those who fear the next life

row.title: those who fear
sub: the punishment of the next life

then: The destruction of deniers and rescue of believers is {idea}a sign for those who fear the punishment of the Hereafter{/idea}. It points to a Day when all people, the first and last, are gathered. Ibn Kathir says angels and messengers will be present, and {reward}the Most Just will not wrong anyone by an atom's weight{/reward}.
now: You stand in a packed stadium, or the crowd at Eid prayer, and feel small among thousands. {idea}Imagine every human ever, in one place.{/idea} Everyone seen. That thought can make your private choices feel very public.
old: What I do in private stays private.
new: There is a Day when everyone is gathered and everything is seen, so I live with that in view.
try: In the next crowd you are part of, remember the Day of gathering and make a quiet dua for it.

title: The Day is delayed only to a counted term.
subtitle: Not a minute more, not a minute less
then: The Day just described is not cancelled by being far away. {idea}Allah only delays it to a counted term{/idea}, a fixed time, as Ibn Kathir says, that {trap}cannot be increased or decreased{/trap}.
now: The deadline is months away, so you do not start. Then it is next week. {idea}A counted term is already counting.{/idea} Your own days are numbered the same way; every one used is one fewer.
old: There is plenty of time before I need to get serious.
new: My days and the Day are both counted, so I use the time I have now.
try: Do today one good thing you keep putting off for "later."

title: No one speaks except by His leave.
subtitle: A silent Day that splits into two
then: On that Day {idea}no soul will speak except by Allah's permission{/idea}. In the hadith of intercession, the Prophet ﷺ said even the messengers will only say: O Allah, save us, save us. People will be {trap}wretched{/trap} or {reward}happy{/reward}. Umar asked if it depended on deeds; the Prophet ﷺ said each person is eased toward what he was created for.
now: You are used to explaining yourself: to HR, to your parents, in the comments. You can usually talk your way through. {idea}On that Day, words are by permission only.{/idea} What speaks for you is what you did today.
old: I can always explain myself later.
new: On that Day my deeds speak, not my excuses, so I let them speak well now.
try: Do one good deed today quietly, without telling anyone, and let it speak for you later.

title: The wretched will be in the Fire, gasping.
subtitle: A sober glimpse of the losing side
then: Allah describes the wretched in the Fire. Ibn Abbas explained the two words as {trap}hard sounds of breathing out and breathing in{/trap}, from the distress they feel. Ibn Kathir adds: {idea}we seek refuge with Allah from such evil{/idea}.
now: You take an easy breath right now without thinking. In a hard workout, or a panic attack, you learn what it is to struggle for air. {idea}Every easy breath is a gift and a chance.{/idea} Use it to turn toward Him.
old: Thinking about the Fire is too heavy; better to avoid it.
new: Allah describes it so I seek refuge and change course while I still can.
try: After your next prayer, say: O Allah, protect me from the Fire, three times.

title: As long as the heavens and earth endure.
subtitle: Lasting, except what your Lord wills
then: Ibn Jarir said the Arabs used "as long as the heavens and earth endure" to mean forever. Then comes {reward}except what your Lord wills{/reward}. Many scholars said this refers to sinful believers in tawhid, brought out by intercession, and even those whose only good was {reward}saying La ilaha illallah{/reward}.
now: You feel your sins are too many to ever be forgiven. Your record feels like a debt you cannot pay. {reward}The one word of tawhid carries enormous weight.{/reward} Hold on to it, and build on it.
old: If I have sinned badly, there is no hope left for me.
new: Allah does what He wills, and His mercy reaches even those with very little good, if they held to tawhid.
try: Say La ilaha illallah slowly and sincerely ten times today, thinking about its meaning.

title: A gift that is never cut off.
subtitle: The happy ones in Paradise, forever
then: The blessed, the followers of the messengers, will be in Paradise forever. Ibn Kathir says Allah ended with {reward}a gift without an end{/reward} so no one would think it could stop. The Prophet ﷺ said the people of Paradise will be told they will {reward}live and never die, stay young, healthy and never grieve{/reward}.
now: The holiday ends, the new phone gets old, the best day is followed by Monday. Every joy here has an expiry date. {reward}Imagine one that never does.{/reward} That is what your small good deeds are aimed at.
old: Every happiness eventually runs out.
new: The joy Allah promises the believers is a gift that never ends.
try: When a good moment ends today, say: O Allah, give me the joy that never ends.

title: They worship only what their fathers worshipped.
subtitle: Copying without knowing is no foundation
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ not to doubt that the polytheists' worship is false. Ibn Kathir says {trap}they had no support for it except copying their fathers in ignorance{/trap}. Allah will give everyone their portion in full.
now: You do some things because "our family always does it": the way you spend at weddings, the grudges, even parts of worship you never asked about. {idea}Inherited is not the same as checked.{/idea} Keep what is true, question what is only habit.
old: If my family has always done it, it must be right.
new: I need to know why I do what I do, not just that my elders did it.
try: Pick one family custom and look up whether it truly has a basis in the deen.

title: Musa's Book was disputed too.
subtitle: Comfort for the Prophet ﷺ facing denial
then: Allah reminds the Prophet ﷺ that {idea}He gave Musa the Book, and people differed over it{/idea}. So he has an example in earlier prophets and should not grieve. Ibn Jarir said that {trap}if the judgment had not been delayed to a set time{/trap}, it would have been decided immediately.
now: You share something true and beneficial and get mocked, or ignored, by your own family. You wonder if you said it wrong. {idea}Even revealed Books were argued over.{/idea} Rejection does not make the truth less true.
old: If people argue against the truth I share, I must have failed.
new: Disagreement over truth is an old pattern; my job is to stay patient and sincere.
try: When someone rejects a good word from you today, let it go without bitterness.

title: Every one of them is paid in full.
subtitle: Nothing small or great is overlooked

row.title: everything
sub: small and great, fine and ugly

then: Allah will gather the early and later generations and {idea}repay each of them their deeds in full{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says He knows all of them: {reward}their honorable deeds{/reward} and {trap}their despicable deeds{/trap}, the small and the great.
now: The extra minute you stayed to help a coworker. The snide remark in the family group. The coin you gave without anyone seeing. {idea}None of it is lost.{/idea} That is a warning and a huge comfort at once.
old: Small acts, good or bad, do not really count.
new: Allah knows every small deed and repays it fully, so nothing good I do is wasted.
try: Do one tiny good deed today that no one will notice, trusting that He does.

title: Stand straight as you were commanded.
subtitle: Steadiness without going beyond the limits

row.title: the Prophet ﷺ
sub: and those who turned with him

then: After all the stories, Allah commands the Prophet ﷺ and the believers with him to {idea}stand firm and upright, as commanded{/idea}. Ibn Kathir says this is a great help against opposition. He also forbids transgression, which {trap}destroys the one who does it, even against a polytheist{/trap}. Allah sees all they do.
now: You start strong in Ramadan, then crash. Or you get angry online and go further than truth allows. {idea}Straight is steady, not extreme.{/idea} Keep the line, every day, and do not cross it even when provoked.
old: Being religious means going as hard as I can.
new: Allah asks me to stay straight and steady, and never cross limits, even with those I oppose.
try: Choose one small act of worship you can keep daily, and keep it the same size all week.

title: Do not lean toward those who do wrong.
subtitle: Small compromises with wrong add up
then: Ibn Abbas explained the verse: {trap}do not compromise with them, do not side with those who do wrong{/trap}. Ibn Kathir adds: do not seek their help, as if approving their evil. Otherwise {idea}you will have no protector besides Allah{/idea} and no one to help you.
now: Your friend is running a dodgy scheme and asks you to just "vouch for him." Your boss wants your quiet support for something unfair. {trap}Leaning starts small.{/trap} You can be kind to people and still refuse to prop up what they are doing wrong.
old: As long as I am not the one doing wrong, supporting it a little is fine.
new: Leaning on wrongdoing, even quietly, pulls me toward it; Allah is my only real protector.
try: Decline one request today that would mean quietly backing something you know is wrong.

title: Good deeds wash away bad ones.
subtitle: Prayer through the day as a cleansing river
then: Ibn Mas'ud reported that a man who had kissed a woman not lawful to him came to the Prophet ﷺ, ashamed. This verse came: {idea}establish prayer at both ends of the day and in the night{/idea}, for {reward}good deeds remove misdeeds{/reward}. He asked if it was only for him. The Prophet ﷺ said it was for all his community.
now: You said something cruel this afternoon, or looked at something you should not have. Now you feel too dirty to pray. {reward}That is exactly when to pray.{/reward} The Prophet ﷺ compared the five prayers to a river at your door you bathe in five times a day.
old: After I sin, I should stay away from prayer until I feel worthy.
new: Prayer and good deeds are how Allah washes my sins away, so I go to them right after a slip.
try: The next time you slip today, make wudu and pray two rakat right away.

title: Be patient; no good effort is ever lost.
subtitle: Patience alongside prayer
then: Right after the command to pray, Allah says {idea}be patient{/idea}. The believers in Makkah faced rejection and pressure every day. {reward}Allah does not let the reward of those who do good be lost.{/reward}
now: You keep showing up: caring for an ill parent, raising a child alone, working an honest job that pays less. Months pass with no thanks. {reward}Not one hour is wasted.{/reward} Patience is trusting that it is all being kept.
old: If my efforts go unnoticed, they were pointless.
new: Allah keeps every good effort I make, so my patience is never wasted.
try: Write down one hard thing you keep doing for Allah's sake, and remind yourself: none of it is lost.

title: If only a few had spoken up against corruption.
subtitle: The missing voices in the past nations
then: Allah asks why there were not, among earlier generations, {idea}people of wisdom who forbade corruption on earth{/idea}, except a few whom He saved. The wrongdoers {trap}chased the luxuries they were given{/trap}. Ibn Kathir says this is why this community is told to always have people who call to good and forbid evil.
now: Someone in the office shares a cruel joke about a colleague. Your cousin is cheating his business partner and everyone knows. {idea}One calm voice matters.{/idea} Silence feels safe, but the few who spoke were the ones saved.
old: It is not my place to say anything when others do wrong.
new: A few people willing to speak gently against wrong can protect a whole community.
try: When you see something wrong today, say one kind, clear sentence about it instead of staying silent.

title: He would never destroy a town of reformers.
subtitle: Reformers protect the places they live in
then: Allah says He {idea}would not destroy towns unjustly while their people were reformers{/idea}. Ibn Kathir explains that no punishment comes to a town unless its people wronged themselves, and {reward}your Lord is not unjust to His servants{/reward}.
now: Your street, your workplace, your family group. Someone has to be the one who fixes, forgives, picks up litter, settles the quarrel. {reward}Reformers protect the places they live in.{/reward} You can be one of them.
old: What happens to my community has nothing to do with me.
new: When people work to set things right, they become a protection for the place they live.
try: Do one small repair in your community today: settle a dispute, clean a space, help a neighbor.

title: He could have made everyone one community.
subtitle: Why people keep differing
then: Allah says that {idea}had He willed, He could have made mankind one community{/idea}, all upon belief. Ibn Kathir says instead {trap}people will always differ in religions, creeds and opinions{/trap}. This comes after a whole surah of nations that chose differently from their prophets.
now: You look at your family and see every view under one roof: devout, doubting, indifferent. It frustrates you. {idea}Difference was allowed for a reason.{/idea} Choice is real, which means your own choice to follow guidance really counts.
old: If Allah wanted everyone guided, nobody would disagree.
new: Allah allowed people to differ so that choosing guidance is a real choice, including mine.
try: In your next disagreement about faith, focus on your own choice to follow guidance rather than on winning.

title: Except those your Lord has shown mercy.
subtitle: The way out of endless division

row.title: following the Prophet ﷺ
sub: what he and his Companions were upon

then: People will keep differing {reward}except those your Lord has shown mercy{/reward}. Ibn Kathir says these are the ones who follow the messengers and what they commanded. Asked who the saved group are, the Prophet ﷺ said: {idea}those upon what I and my Companions are upon{/idea}. And {trap}Allah's word that He will fill Hell{/trap} will be fulfilled.
now: Online, everyone is in a camp, fighting over labels and personalities. You feel the pull to pick a side and defend it. {idea}Mercy is in following the Prophet ﷺ{/idea}, not in winning the group argument.
old: The right group is the one I already belong to.
new: Mercy comes from following what the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions were upon, not from loyalty to a camp.
try: Before sharing a religious opinion online, check what the Prophet ﷺ actually said on it.

title: These stories were told to steady your heart.
subtitle: Why the surah gathered all these prophets
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ that He related all these stories of the messengers {idea}to make his heart firm{/idea}. They show how the prophets were rejected and harmed, and how Allah helped the believers. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said "in this" means this surah: it brings {reward}the truth, an admonition, and a reminder for the believers{/reward}.
now: You feel alone in trying to live your faith: the only one praying at the office, the only one in the family who fasts. {idea}Read the stories again.{/idea} Nuh, Hud, Salih, Shu'ayb, Musa all stood where you stand, and they were helped.
old: No one has ever faced what I am facing.
new: The prophets faced it before me, and their stories are there to steady my heart.
try: Reread one prophet's story from this surah tonight and note one thing that steadies you.

title: Keep to your way. We are working on ours.
subtitle: The Prophet ﷺ echoes the prophets before him
then: Allah tells the Prophet ﷺ to say to the deniers what Shu'ayb said earlier: {trap}act according to your way{/trap}, {idea}we are acting on ours{/idea}. Ibn Kathir calls it a warning, and notes that Allah fulfilled His promise and helped His Messenger ﷺ.
now: Your relatives tease you every Eid about how "strict" you have become. You have explained, more than once. {idea}Now you just keep going.{/idea} Your consistency is your answer.
old: I have to convince everyone before I can be at peace with my choices.
new: Once I have spoken clearly, I can simply keep working on my path and let time show.
try: Skip one argument today and instead do one good deed you were going to do anyway.

title: Wait, and we are waiting too.
subtitle: Calm waiting for how things end
then: The command continues: {idea}wait, we too are waiting{/idea}. Ibn Kathir links it to the verse that the wrongdoers will not succeed. He says {reward}Allah fulfilled His promise to His Messenger ﷺ{/reward}, helped him, and made His word uppermost.
now: You are waiting for the job offer, the test result, the reconciliation with a sibling. Waiting can eat you up. {reward}A believer's waiting is calm{/reward}, because it is waiting on a promise from One who keeps His word.
old: Waiting means sitting in anxiety until things work out.
new: I can wait calmly, because I am waiting on Allah, who keeps His promises.
try: While you wait on something today, replace one anxious thought with: Allah keeps His promise.

title: Every matter returns to Him; worship and trust Him.
subtitle: The last words of Surah Hud
then: Surah Hud ends here. {idea}To Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth{/idea}, and every matter returns to Him. So worship Him and rely on Him. Ibn Kathir says {reward}He is sufficient for whoever trusts and turns to Him{/reward}, and nothing anyone does is hidden from Him.
now: You close the app after a heavy surah full of floods, cries and ruins. Your own worries are still there: rent, kids, health. {reward}Hand them over.{/reward} Worship Him, trust Him, and know He sees every effort you make.
old: I have to carry all of my worries and hold everything together myself.
new: Everything returns to Allah, so I worship Him, rely on Him, and trust He sees what I do.
try: Tonight, name your three biggest worries to Allah in dua and say: I rely on You.
